summary: Tower built in 1936 to watch the new Feather River highway near Belden; a lookout was on duty in 1944; FFLA lists it gone.

facts.design: Tower with a 14-by-14-foot room planned at the top, on 16-by-16-foot foundations
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source gives a removal date or describes what remains.

access.note: No source says whether the site is open to visitors.

events.note: Under construction in July 1936 with foundations laid; a September 1936 paper expected it finished the following week.
Reported as linked to the telephone system; CCC enrollees from Camp Concow were to build the new line.
Freda Danielson, a Plumas National Forest lookout, had been on duty about two months and had killed three wildcats and seven rattlesnakes.

evidence.supports: Built to watch the highway route, from a point near Belden
evidence.quote: Located especially to watch the highway route, the Bear Ranch Hill lookout station is now under construction at a point near Belden.

evidence.supports: Placed at the edge of a sheer cliff near the highway, on the Butte-Plumas boundary
evidence.quote: The lookout has been placed at the edge of a sheer cliff near the highway on the Butte-Plumas county boundary line.

evidence.supports: Highway not yet open; lookout to watch traffic once it opens
evidence.quote: will watch all traffic on the new Feather river highway when it is opened next year

evidence.supports: Foundation and top-room dimensions (plans); foundations already laid in the 29 July 1936 article
evidence.quote: Foundations of the tower have already been laid. The foundations are 16 by 16 feet and the room at the top of the tower will be 14 by 14 feet.
The Bear Ranch Hill lookout near Brush Creek will be completed next week.

evidence.supports: Linked to the telephone system (1938 report)
evidence.quote: A new lookout station established last year at Bear Ranch Hill is linked with the telephone system.

evidence.supports: Freda Danielson was the Plumas National Forest lookout on Bear Ranch Hill in 1944
evidence.quote: Freda Danielson, Plumas National Forest lookout on Bear Ranch Hill

evidence.supports: About two months on duty by August 1944; three wildcats and seven rattlesnakes killed
evidence.quote: In the two months Mrs. Danielson has been serving as a Forest lookout she has killed three wild cats and seven rattle snakes.

evidence.supports: Listed as gone, tower, Butte County
Station overlooks a section of the Feather River Canyon (1944 account)
evidence.quote: Her station is on a rocky promontory which overlooks a section of the Feather River Canyon.

evidence.supports: Telephone line to be built by CCC enrollees from Camp Concow (Dec 1938 report)
evidence.quote: Construction of the new line will be done by CCC enrollees from Camp Concow.

evidence.supports: The 1944 account was reported by D.K. Carr, Forest Service Training Officer
evidence.quote: was reported this week by D.K. Carr, Forest Service Training Officer

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 29 December 1938 report calls the station 'established last year' (1937). The 29 July 1936 and 3 September 1936 papers describe it under construction and nearly finished, so the story keeps 1936 as the build date.

notes_for_editor: History comes from one page (Forest Lookouts) that quotes 1936-1944 newspapers; I could not open the newspapers themselves. No removal date or site description found, so the story says only that FFLA lists it gone and that no source describes the site today. Staffing fact is historical (1944), not current. The FFLA row has no register number; numbers printed just above the row in the text belong to Bear Mountain (Fresno County). Brief record has no register entries, so nothing to correct.
